dedupe_keys.name: seawater intrusion and infiltration modelling coupled to digital tools to avoid high saline concentrations in reclaimed water application in coastal central italy

description: The documented workflow couples dynamic seawater-intrusion and runoff simulation with a smart-equalization control algorithm and a matchmaking decision tool. It predicts salinity peaks and allocates wastewater or reclaimed water between industrial use, irrigation and conventional or reverse-osmosis treatment. The source reports a coastal central-Italy simulation with conductivity of 2,100–2,700 microsiemens per centimetre and allocation of 71 percent to industry, 10 percent to irrigation and 19 percent to discharge. These are results of the described scenario, not year-round recovery guarantees. The abstract calls its simulated period "2D" without an unambiguous duration definition. A supplement lists measurement campaigns, calibration and model-performance sections; executable components and complete inputs remain unknown. The source documents a water quality treatment or recovery study. The source authors provide this description through Zenodo, whose deposit declares CC BY 4.0 and public document access. Geographic and temporal coverage remain limited to the cases or observations explicitly described. Only metadata and file descriptors were reviewed; no document, measurements, model archive or code was read. Related components retain their source identities and uncertain experimental overlap. Document access and licensing do not establish executable availability or software rights.
